purpose: Teach: 元年/時空/界隈/特質/総称/現存/波長/即興

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、明治元年の改革史を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Ren, I see you wrote your paper on the history of reforms in the Meiji era.
lines.style: Open with gentle curiosity. Warm, professorial tone. Calm pace with a slight upward lilt at the end—inviting confirmation, not demanding it.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、相対性理論の時空概念を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes, I wrote mine on the spacetime concepts in relativity theory.
lines.style: Quiet, slightly hurried delivery. Eager to answer correctly. Keeps eye contact brief. A hint of nervous energy beneath the politeness.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、銀座界隈の商業史を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: And Ren, your paper explored the commercial history of the Ginza area, didn't it?
lines.style: Reflective pause before speaking. Thoughtful tone, slightly tilted head. Gentle assumption phrased as a question—giving him room to correct her.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、漢字の音声的特質を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Actually, mine focused on the phonetic characteristics of kanji.
lines.style: Soft correction, not defensive. Matter-of-fact but respectful. Even pace. Small exhale before answering—a moment of clarifying what was misunderstood.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 動植物の総称分類を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: I remember you engaging quite deeply with the taxonomic classification of flora and fauna.
lines.style: Brighter tone than before. Warm recognition. Slight lean forward—this one genuinely impressed her. Eyes warm with acknowledgment.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、現存最古の文献研究を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Thank you. I actually researched the earliest existing written records instead.
lines.style: Grateful nod in his voice. A touch less nervous than before. Steady pace. The 'actually' is gentle, not corrective—just clarifying for her benefit.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、超音波の波長解析を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Your paper on ultrasonic wavelength analysis was quite thorough, wasn't it?
lines.style: Reflective and searching. Slower pace. A slight frown in her voice—this doesn't quite match what she recalls. Genuinely trying to piece it together.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、ジャズの即興演奏研究を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Thank you, but I actually wrote on improvisation techniques in jazz.
lines.style: Soft, genuine. A quiet smile underneath. He's gotten used to these mismatches now. Patient, almost resigned kindness in his tone. Warm close.
